issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a StockIngredient constructor with three parameters (String, int, int), but the template provides a constructor with an extra boolean parameter (String, int, int, boolean). This mismatch will confuse students about the correct constructor signature and may prevent them from instantiating StockIngredient as shown in the problem examples and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Add or restore a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) in the template (or provide an overload) so the template matches the problem statement and the solution. Alternatively, adjust the problem statement/examples to use the four-argument constructor if the boolean/configuration parameter is intentional.

issues.description: Within the template repository, the Main class (commented example code) constructs StockIngredient using a three-argument constructor (StockIngredient(String, int, int)), but the template's StockIngredient class only defines a four-argument constructor (with a boolean). This internal inconsistency will cause compilation errors for students who try to run or follow the example Main code.
issues.suggestedFix: Either update the example calls in Main to pass the boolean fourth argument required by the template constructor, or (preferably) add a three-argument constructor overload StockIngredient(String, int, int) to the template so the example code and the problem statement align and compile correctly.
